identity_marker: chrome Hansgrohe Metris single-hole bathroom faucet with a flat metal handle and cylindrical brass body
continuity_anchors: set against a clean white porcelain bathroom sink under bright, even overhead bathroom lighting
video_goal: Demonstrate the step-by-step process of removing and replacing the ceramic disc cartridge in a Hansgrohe Metris faucet.
single_prompt: A first-person view shows hands reaching under a clean white porcelain bathroom sink under bright, even overhead bathroom lighting to turn two oval water supply valve handles clockwise until they stop. The camera moves to a close-up as a small metal pick is inserted into the small seam of the red/blue temperature indicator plug on the front of the chrome Hansgrohe Metris single-hole bathroom faucet with a flat metal handle and cylindrical brass body, popping the plug out. In an extreme close-up, a 2.5mm Allen wrench is inserted into the exposed hole and rotated counter-clockwise multiple times. From an eye-level view, a hand grasps the flat metal handle and pulls it straight up, separating it from the faucet body. An over-the-shoulder view shows fingers gripping the smooth, dome-shaped metal cap below the handle and twisting it counter-clockwise to remove it. The camera shifts to a close-up as an adjustable wrench is fitted around the exposed brass retaining nut and pushed counter-clockwise to break it loose. Returning to a first-person view, fingers spin the loosened brass retaining nut off and lift it away. In a close-up, fingers pinch the plastic stem of the old ceramic disc cartridge and pull it straight up and out. From a high-angle close-up, a microfiber cloth is pushed into the empty brass faucet body, wiping the metal base and two circular water inlet holes. A close-up shows a hand holding up a new Hansgrohe ceramic disc cartridge, tilting the bottom to reveal two protruding plastic alignment pegs. From an over-the-shoulder view, the new cartridge is lowered into the faucet body, twisting slightly until the bottom pegs drop into the alignment holes. In a close-up, the brass retaining nut is threaded back over the cartridge by hand, then tightened firmly with the adjustable wrench. An eye-level view captures the decorative dome cap being screwed back on by hand, and the flat metal handle pressed down onto the new cartridge stem. Finally, in a close-up, the Allen wrench tightens the set screw clockwise, the red/blue plug is pushed back into the hole, and the handle is lifted to show water flowing.
